lifecycle._doc: Post-hoc maintenance via mail-sieve-subset-post-hoc.sh. SQL-direct on /data/imapsql.db using the actual go-imap-sql schema. UNIFIED-INBOX delivery model: maddy delivery-time always places mail in INBOX (with \Seen via inbox_copy_flags from mail-rules.json); apply-rules then SQL-direct COPIES (NOT moves) into matched category folders with rule-derived keywords (no \Seen — copies are unread). INBOX is the chronological archive; category folders are the unread working set. apply-rules is idempotent via the $distributed keyword on the INBOX original — maddy-sorter (src/crate, Rust, compiled into this same image via docker.native_build) runs the equivalent logic continuously (started by init.sh alongside `maddy run`, no external scheduler); the bash cmd_apply_rules / post-hoc-apply-rules lifecycle entries below are for manual/testing use only now. reseed-inbox-archive is a one-shot history backfill that COPIES every existing non-system folder msg back into INBOX as \Seen + $distributed (Message-Id deduped). recover-headers stays intentionally NOT a subcommand: missing-blob bodies are unrecoverable, integrity-fix is the right action.

l4_ports.comment: SMTP MX plain TCP — design-complete listener; GCP firewall currently blocks public, CF Worker is the active inbound bridge

primary._doc_l4_ports: Only :25 lives here — Maddy still answers plain SMTP. The imap./smtps. SNI routes on :443 moved to user-comm_tools-stalwart/build.json, which is what actually terminates them (:2993/:2465). A route is declared by the service that answers the bytes.

app._doc_dual_bind: Phase 4 of public-surface collapse: each port dual-binds on wg0 (10.0.0.3) AND wg-public (10.1.0.3). Maddy is host-network so binds happen inside maddy.conf.tpl via `@LISTEN_<port>@`; flake.nix expands `bind` arrays into space-separated multi-listener prefixes (e.g. `tls://10.0.0.3:993 tls://10.1.0.3:993`). Caddy on oci-analytics reaches mail ports via wg-public; legacy clients on wg0 keep working unchanged.

extra_ports.desc: MX delivery endpoint — dual-bind wg0+wg-public; CF Worker → Caddy → http-to-smtp-proxy-api → SMTP over WG is the public bridge (Phase 5)
SMTPS — dual-bind wg0+wg-public, reached via Caddy L4 from oci-analytics
IMAPS — dual-bind wg0+wg-public, reached via Caddy L4 from oci-analytics

docker._doc: Was Type-B (FROM foxcpp/maddy:0.9 + apk add, no compile). Now native_build: same base image (still gets maddy itself for free from upstream), same apk packages (moved from runtime_packages -- that field only fed the Type-B auto-detect path, which native_build.type bypasses entirely), PLUS an in-container compile of maddy-sorter (src/crate) copied in alongside. One image, both binaries -- maddy-sorter's own code lives in this service's src/, same as jmap-sorter does for Stalwart.

native_build._doc_builder_image: MUST be an alpine/musl builder, not rust:1-bookworm (glibc) -- base_image below is foxcpp/maddy:0.9 (alpine/musl). A glibc-linked binary copied into a musl final image has no dynamic linker to run against (this isn't a PATH issue patchelf can fix, unlike the nix-store-ld-linux case elsewhere in this repo -- glibc and musl are different libcs, not just different paths to the same one). rust:1-alpine's native target already IS x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, so no --target flag or cross toolchain needed, just a C compiler for libsqlite3-sys's build script (rusqlite's "bundled" feature compiles its own sqlite3.c) -- hence build-base in cmd below.
native_build._doc_apk: jq/sqlite/coreutils are for the OTHER post-hoc subcommands (integrity-check, dedupe, cleanup-mailboxes, reseed-inbox-archive), which stay bash + sqlite3-CLI. maddy-sorter itself needs neither -- rusqlite's bundled feature compiles its own libsqlite3, no apk sqlite required for apply-rules specifically.
